claims.text: Multicomponent high-entropy-alloy liquids exhibit many diverse atomic configurations.
Conventional EAM references inadequately represent the configurations of the ab initio liquid.
The EAM reference should be replaced by an MLIP in free-energy perturbation or thermodynamic-integration calculations.
The MLIP should be trained on a representative ab initio dataset of liquid configurations.
Training on liquid configurations enables the MLIP to capture relevant many-body interactions.
An MLIP trained on ab initio liquid configurations will represent liquid-phase atomic interactions more accurately than a conventional EAM reference.
The improved interaction representation will increase phase-space overlap between the reference and target ab initio ensembles.
Capturing a broader range of many-body interactions and liquid configurations will reduce mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration pathway.
Reducing insufficient phase-space overlap will reduce free-energy integration errors.
The MLIP reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 30–50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The reduced integration-path mismatch will produce more accurate free-energy results.
The proposed method is expected to apply primarily to near-equimolar multicomponent high-entropy alloys at or near their melting temperatures.
The method may be less effective far from the near-melting regime or for systems with markedly different bonding characteristics.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant mismatch reduction relative to the EAM control would falsify the hypothesis.
